correctness.rationale: After the exact substitution \(t=((-\log y)/\lambda)^k\), the Rényi integral is a positive constant times \(\int_0^\infty t^{(p-1)(k-1)/k} e^{(p-1)\lambda t^{1/k}-pt/2}(1-e^{-t})^{-p/2}dt\). At zero the exact integrability condition is \(k>2-2/p\); at infinity the tail is always finite for \(0<p<1\), finite for \(p>1,k>1\), infinite for \(p>1,k<1\), and for \(k=1\) finite exactly when \(\lambda<p/[2(p-1)]\). Combining the endpoint conditions gives the stated necessary-and-sufficient classification, with strict boundary divergence.

value.rationale: The result supplies the exact existence domain for an information measure presented as a statistical property of a new 2026 model. It is materially relevant to the paper’s own application because the reported maximum-likelihood shape \(k=0.9952<1\) forces divergence for every Rényi order \(p>1\). The finding separates a genuine information-theoretic limitation from the otherwise valid probability model and estimation procedure.
